reading.body:
Consensus is an AI academic search engine for peer-reviewed literature, and the available record contains no lawsuits, MCP servers, SEC filings, or patents for it.

The company is tracked as a single product, a research search tool, described on its own site as a research operating system for finding, organizing, and analyzing science faster. That is the whole of the profile. There is no funding history, no headcount, no infrastructure disclosure, and no customer list in the data.

For AI specifically, this places Consensus at the application layer rather than the compute layer. Nothing here describes training runs, accelerators, data centers, or power contracts, so the data cannot speak to how much compute the product consumes or where it runs. A search product over published literature may be far lighter on inference than a frontier model, but that is an inference from the product category, not a fact the record establishes.

What the data does not cover is most of what would make the company legible as an AI business. It gives a website, a verification date, a category, and a short self-description. It says nothing about scale, revenue, model providers, or the physical footprint behind the service.

The product tracked under the Consensus name is a research search tool. No lawsuits, MCP servers, SEC filings, or patent records are associated with the company in the available material.
